region.text: the oases of Khotan, from Niya to the Kashgar side

ledger.note: 851: Khotan regains its independence from Tibet. 'Khotan was taken by the Tibetan Empire in 792' and 'would go on to gain its independence in 851'. The page names the kingdom, not a boundary; the shape is Cliopatria's 888 shape.

970: Khotan takes Kashgar. 'Khotan briefly took Kashgar from the Kara-Khanids in 970.' Tarim Basin page: 'Halfway in the 10th century Khotan came under attack by the Karakhanid ruler Musa' and a long war followed.
971: Kashgar back with the Kara-Khanids (bridging): the page says only 'briefly' and dates no return; 971 is the next dated entry (a letter from the king of Khotan to the Chinese emperor).

1006: Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquers Khotan. 'In 1006, the Muslim Kara-Khanid ruler Yusuf Kadir (Qadir) Khan of Kashgar conquered Khotan, ending its existence as an independent state'; 'Khotan held by the Muslim Yūsuf Qadr Khān, a brother or cousin of the Muslim ruler of Kāshgar and Balāsāghūn'.
1006: the Kingdom of Khotan ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 1006'). Cliopatria draws it to 1009; the last king listed is Viśa' Sagemayi (999-1006).

wars.name: Khotan-Kara-Khanid war
wars.outcome: Khotan came under attack by the Karakhanid ruler Musa halfway in the 10th century; it briefly took Kashgar in 970; the war 'eventually ended in the conquest of Khotan by Kashgar by the Karakhanid leader Yusuf Qadir Khan around 1006'.
wars.note: The start is the Tarim Basin page's 'halfway in the 10th century' (c. 950), a bracket; the Kingdom of Khotan page dates only 970 and 1006.

certainty.note: A string of oases in the southern Tarim; no page gives the extent in this period, and the frontier with Kashgar moved with the Kara-Khanid wars.

notes:
Pages opened: Kingdom of Khotan (twice), Tarim Basin, plus the Kara-Khanid Khanate and Tibetan Empire pages opened for the neighbours (4 distinct pages, budget 5).
Start: the infobox gives 'Established c. 300 BC'; Cliopatria draws the kingdom only from 888 and the pages that I opened give the Tibetan years (665/670, 692, 792) and the 851 independence but no extents. This dossier starts at 851, the independence year, and does not map the kingdom before the Tibetan conquest (the page has Tang submission in 640, the Four Garrisons of Anxi, the 728 title 'King of Khotan' for Yuchi Fushizhan, 756 Yuchi Yao, 786-788 still ruling); a gap-filler should extend it to c. 300 BC and add the Tibetan occupation 792-851 and the earlier Tibetan years as occupation events.
Cliopatria's 888 start is not explained by any page (independence 851); the 1009 end is three years after the page's 1006.
Extent: no page gives the extent of the kingdom in 851-1006. The Cliopatria shape reaches Kashgar and Aksu and the Alay foothills; only Kashgar is corrected (the Kara-Khanids take Kashgar in 934 on the Kara-Khanid page and Khotan 'briefly took' it in 970), and the Kara-Khanid dossier (this batch) uses the same reading with counterpart nobody for 934. Who held Kashgar in 851-933 is not on the pages. The Kyrgyz cells and Aksu are kept as unverified.
Disagreement: the Kara-Khanid page has Satuq's conversion in 934 (932, 960), the Tarim Basin page 966. Rulers: the king list has one year per king; read as start years (Viśa' Saṃbhava 'starting in 912' on the page), so ends are the next start; the page also has a 969 mission by Saṃbhava's son, after the list's 967.
Missing: Khotan's tribute to the Song (969 mission, 971 letter) and the Guiyi marriage alliance of 934 are noted but not mapped; no dated clash between 971 and 1006.
